content:
We have heard rumors from multiple sources about Apple's next-generation iPad mini, including the adoption of an OLED display and improved water resistance.

A new leak today reveals that the upcoming iPad mini will pack powerful specifications: an all-new A20 Pro chip.

MacRumors today discovered references to a new iPad mini in Apple's code, including an icon that appears to represent the device.

The icon shows that the overall design of the new iPad mini will be similar to the existing model. However, the camera has been moved from the top bezel to one side in landscape orientation, aligning with Apple's other iPad models. A small speaker opening has also been added to the top of the display, similar to the iPhone design.

The code also reveals that the new iPad mini will feature an A20 Pro chip, the same chip used in the iPhone 18 Pro series launched last week. The currently available iPad mini was released in October 2024 with an Apple A17 Pro chip.

According to Mark Gurman, the new iPad mini is expected to go on sale before the end of October. In addition to the above changes, the new machine is reportedly set to offer better water resistance and an all-new speaker system.

For more details, you can refer to our complete preview roundup of the new iPad mini.

In another report today, the specifications of the next-generation base-model iPad have also been revealed, including the A19 chip, 8GB of memory, as well as Apple's self-developed N1 and C1X connectivity chips.
